vehicleUpdates.summary: A roomy AWD wagon with a long boot. A related 2021 Sport test fitted one rear-facing and two forward-facing restraints. Centre booster compatibility and your own combination still need checking.

consumption.basis: Australian ADR 81/02 combined laboratory figure for the naturally aspirated 2.5. Separate from XT 9.0 and from observed use.

observedConsumption.basis: CarsGuide exact 2021 base AWD: reviewer average over one week of city, suburban and brief highway driving. Route-specific observation, not a fleet average; the article’s automatic 2.0D data box is inconsistent with its explicitly identified 2.5 petrol test.

boot.basis: Rear seats occupied; VDA volume identified in the exact Australian base AWD family test. Pram shape and loading under the cargo blind still matter.

length.basis: Australian BT base specification, excluding accessories; not the seventh-generation MY26 Outback.

width.basis: Australian BT specification excluding mirrors; width alone does not establish three-restraint fit.

towing.basis: Maximum braked trailer mass for non-XT 2.5 with suitable equipment; 200 kg maximum tow-ball download and vehicle/axle/load limits still apply. Do not use XT 2,400 kg.

vehicleUpdates.warranty: 5 years / unlimited km for private use from original first registration; transferable subject to terms. 12 V battery cover is 2 years. Confirm remaining cover by VIN.
vehicleUpdates.servicing: Non-XT: 12 months / 12,500 km, whichever first. First five capped visits: MY21 A$2,449.88; MY25 A$2,715.67. Older used cars need a quote for the actual next services.

safety.applicability: BT generation, all variants built from December 2020; Australian sale from March 2021, expiry December 2027. Report updated December 2022. Does not establish a rating for seventh-generation MY26.

familyFit.summary: Related 2021 Sport: one rear-facing plus two forward-facing seats fitted. Centre belt routing was awkward; ANCAP could not safely fit either selected centre booster. Check your exact arrangement in this base grade.
familyFit.row2: Two outer ISOFIX pairs and three rear-seatback top tethers. Centre installation uses the roof-mounted vehicle belt. ANCAP’s selected harnessed seats fitted individually across the rear row; its two selected boosters failed in the centre.
familyFit.testedSeats: BabyDrive 2021 Sport: rear-facing behind the front passenger, two forward-facing restraints including the centre. Article does not name the restraint models; it does not prove any two harnessed seats or boosters will work.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Daily booster buckle access was not established. Test the actual belt receivers and roof-mounted centre belt with all three seats installed.
familyFit.access: The related test found loading a child from inside or outside manageable. Exact base CarsGuide test reports wide-opening doors. BabyDrive front-passenger clearance is inconsistently stated as 182 and 184 cm; use 182 cm as the conservative report, not a measurement for your seat.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear console vents and two rear USB ports; centre armrest cupholders are unavailable with a centre restraint. Base seats/tailgate are manual, unlike some higher grades.

pros: Related mixed-facing three-restraint test with good front clearance.
522 L VDA boot, full-size spare and 2,000 kg braked towing.
Used MY21 base asking prices are below the A$45,000 target.
cons: Selected centre boosters failed ANCAP installation checks; exact seats matter.
12,500 km servicing and relatively high observed city/suburban fuel use.
Touchscreen climate controls and frequent driver-assistance alerts need a test drive.
inspection: Confirm BT sixth-generation base naturally aspirated 2.5; exclude XT, diesel, older-generation and seventh-generation MY26 ads.
Trial one rear-facing and two other restraints independently; check centre belt geometry, every buckle and front-seat clearance. Ask for the VIN-matched Australian owner manual.
Get completion evidence for REC-001227, REC-005005, REC-005830 and MY23 REC-005831 where VIN-applicable.
Check cooling/thermo-control-valve diagnosis or replacement history, CVT operation cold and hot, front suspension bushes and 12 V battery health.
Read dated 12,500 km invoices; obtain a quote for due coolant, differential fluids, spark plugs and fuel filter rather than assuming remaining capped services.
Test the touchscreen, phone connection, climate controls, windscreen and EyeSight operation. MY23 adds wireless phone connectivity and revised controls.

changes.text: Australian BT launch: naturally aspirated 2.5 petrol AWD, 138 kW / 245 Nm, 7.3 L/100km ADR combined. Original base has manual front-seat and tailgate adjustment.

The non-XT mechanical figures remain. MY23 adds wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, front USB-C, revised 11.6-inch screen/climate shortcuts, steering-wheel controls and 18-inch wheel design. The new XT turbo is a separate variant. Verify equipment by model year.
Seventh-generation Outback is outside this BT configuration. Its new-car price, cabin, safety applicability and ownership evidence must be researched separately.

gaps: Two sampled asking cars are MY21; later MY22–MY25 base prices are not established. Cached 2023 stock and a 2022 stock PDF failed fresh availability checks and are excluded.
Restraint models in the 2021 mixed test are unnamed; exact base-grade fit and daily booster buckle access remain pending.
No representative Australian annual repair average or verified installed BT CVT/thermo-control-valve quote found. US warranty extensions do not establish Australian entitlement.
Owner aggregate mixes non-XT and XT grades; no exact base-only rating or failure-rate dataset. Equipment changed for MY23 within this grouped mechanical configuration.

FU34790 advertisement reads A$28,990 drive-away / 54,534 km, but fresh direct fetch returns 403. Cached U63073 and B10215 are excluded after fresh redirect/404 checks. Actual availability and later-year prices remain uncertain.

observations.note: VIN JF2BT9KL3MG005962; stock HW3681. Fresh InStock and asking price confirmed. Cached cashback wording requires seller confirmation; no unconditional quote.
VIN JF2BT9KL3MG010239; stock FU34790. Readable seller advertisement; fresh direct fetch blocked (403), so availability is lower-confidence.

ownershipUpdates.serviceInterval: BT non-XT 2.5 petrol: 12 months or 12,500 km, whichever first. Do not use the XT interval.
ownershipUpdates.serviceBasis: ESTIMATE: A$750/year (A$600–1,100), retained for a used BT at 15,000 km/year. Original MY21 first five caps total A$2,449.88; MY25 A$2,715.67. These are year-specific initial caps, not current post-cap quotes. Distance-scaled references are about A$588 and A$652/year respectively. Allow for ageing cars and due major visits; tyres, wear repairs and accident damage are separate.
warrantyCautions: Five-year private-use cover runs from original first registration and transfers subject to the terms; it does not restart when bought used. Commercial-use limit is five years / 150,000 km.
The 12 V battery has two-year cover. Ordinary suspension/bush, tyre, brake and glass wear or external damage are excluded; a manufacturing defect is a different question.
Dealer mechanical protection and US thermo-control-valve extensions are separate from Australian manufacturer cover. Obtain VIN-specific Australian support before authorising a paid repair.
Australian Consumer Law guarantees remain separate. Ask Subaru to confirm original warranty clock, service eligibility and campaign completion in writing.

risks.title: CVT / AWD drivetrain diagnosis
risks.detail: Inspect cold and hot operation, shudder, warnings, leaks and matching tyres. No Australian BT non-XT failure-rate series or installed major-repair quote was verified. Do not transfer older EJ-engine, diesel or XT faults onto this 2.5.
risks.priceBasis: Quote gap: VIN-specific diagnosis, parts, labour and GST required. A major repair can exceed the saved reserve.
risks.warranty: Manufacturing-defect remedies depend on diagnosis, remaining Australian cover and consumer guarantees; normal wear is different.

risks.title: Thermo-control valve on early cars
risks.detail: A US Subaru bulletin identifies sensor contamination and a revised valve on selected US 2020–22 Outbacks. This is an inspection lead for an early BT, not evidence that every Australian MY21–MY25 is affected.
risks.priceBasis: No verified Australian installed BT repair quote or representative incidence; obtain diagnostic codes and replacement history.
risks.warranty: US 15-year / 150,000-mile cover is not an Australian entitlement. Ask Subaru Australia about the actual VIN and any goodwill.

risks.title: 12 V battery and suspension wear
risks.detail: Check battery condition and front suspension bushes. Owners report problems, but self-selected posts do not establish frequency or a fixed repair price.
risks.priceBasis: Quote gap: inspection and chosen replacement parts determine cost; not an automatic annual repair charge.
risks.warranty: 12 V battery written cover is two years. Ordinary suspension wear is excluded; diagnosis and statutory rights still matter.

risks.title: MY21 EyeSight software recalls
risks.detail: Selected VINs under REC-001227 / SRT306 and REC-005005 / SRT315 may experience unwanted pre-collision braking. Verify both completion records.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 applicable official recall rectification, not a paid-repair forecast.
risks.warranty: Campaign remedy is separate from ordinary warranty expiry.

risks.title: MY21 CVT inhibitor-switch recall
risks.detail: REC-005830 / SRT351 covers 2,610 selected MY21 Outbacks (notice year range 2021–22): moisture may affect reversing lamps/camera. This does not mean the gearbox itself requires replacement.
risks.warranty: Campaign remedy is separate from ordinary warranty expiry.

risks.title: Selected MY23 front-driveshaft recall
risks.detail: REC-005831 / SRT-352 covers 186 Forester/Outback/Crosstrek vehicles combined. A front driveshaft outer race may crack and stop the vehicle. Only the listed VINs apply; this is not 186 Outbacks.
risks.warranty: Authorised Australian Subaru service centres provide campaign rectification.

fuelEstimate.basis: L/100km planning estimate informed by CarsGuide’s exact 2021 base AWD week: 9.6 average for city, suburban and brief highway use. Replaces the previous assumed 9.0 point. The 7.3–11.5 bounds are editorial sensitivity limits, not a statistical interval; highway, load and traffic change use. Official ADR combined 7.3 remains separate. Minimum/planning fuel is 91 RON.

reviewUpdates.scope: ProductReview Australian Outback 6GEN aggregate. Mixed Sport, Touring and Touring XT reviews; no base non-XT-only breakdown. Site labels 2020–2026 and includes a sloppy 2027 alias, so use only as limited related-generation sentiment.
reviewUpdates.summary: Small, self-selected sample with positive comfort/space reports and complaints about alerts, electronics, servicing and support. This is satisfaction evidence, not an Australian failure rate.
positiveThemes: Comfortable long-distance cabin and useful luggage space.
negativeThemes: Intrusive alerts and some infotainment complaints.
Service costs, suspension/battery complaints and variable aftersales experiences.

expertReviews.tested: 2021 Outback AWD base · 2.5 naturally aspirated petrol
expertReviews.scope: Direct Australian base-grade family test; one week of driving, not a long-term reliability study. Body text identifies the petrol base; ignore the mismatched automatic 2.0D specifications box.
expertReviews.verdict: 7.9/10: useful family space, AWD and safety equipment, with relatively high observed fuel use.
positiveThemes: Useful rear-seat and boot space, wide-opening doors and rear vents.
Comfortable family driving and extensive safety equipment.
negativeThemes: 9.6 L/100km in a mostly city/suburban week.
Plain presentation and overly sensitive indicator stalk.

insuranceUpdates.basis: ESTIMATE: Youi national sold-policy Outback mean A$1,138 for 22 Nov 2025–22 May 2026, rounded to A$1140. Mixed years/grades and individual policyholder profiles; no exact Queensland quote, agreed value or new-generation subgroup. Published indicative bands are not confidence intervals; 80% of applicable premiums fell within or below Youi’s bands. Budget bounds are widened editorial sensitivity limits; replace with your quote. Comprehensive cover only; CTP is separately included in registration. The budget and low/high bounds are household planning assumptions, not a personalised quote, insurer minimum/maximum or confidence interval. Address, drivers, excess, insured value and cover can change the premium. Replace with a like-for-like current quote; no arbitrary SUV or generation multiplier is applied.
insuranceUpdates.scope: National model mean · not a 2.5-only sample

tyreUpdates.basis: Budget aftermarket anchor: Radar RPX800+ SUV 104W XL, A$189 each × 4 = A$756 fitted. Ordinary JAX advertised price includes fitting, balancing, tubeless valves, disposal, selected-store delivery and GST; no temporary multi-buy discount used. Store stock and Brisbane availability are unconfirmed. Life is a common 40,000 km planning assumption (25,000–60,000 km sensitivity), not a measured model or tyre average. Wear varies with tyre choice, driving, maintenance and vehicle; model-specific replacement averages were not verified. Annual allowance = set budget × annual km ÷ 40,000, rounded to A$10. Age/damage can require earlier replacement. Alignment is additional; actual placard, wheel package and local fitted quote must be checked. Matching size/load/speed does not establish equal braking, efficiency or durability.

repairReserveUpdates.basis: ESTIMATE: A$1,100/year repair savings budget (A$500–2,400), retained as an editorial allowance for used BT non-XT cooling, electrical, suspension and CVT exposure after original cover. No Australian annual repair average or failure probability establishes this number. Use recall/warranty remedies first. Excludes scheduled services, tyres and insured accident repairs; a major repair may exceed the saved fund.

fitAssessments.summary: 2021 Sport establishes the mixed-facing trial; base-grade installation remains to be checked. Selected centre boosters fail the separate ANCAP check.

arrangement.detail: BabyDrive fitted one rear-facing seat behind the passenger and two forward-facing seats, models unnamed. Centre roof-belt routing was awkward; ANCAP’s selected Type E/F centre boosters could not fit safely.

buckles.detail: No daily mixed-seat booster-buckle access test established. Trial your actual receivers and centre belt with all three fitted.

space.detail: Related test reports good front clearance: at least a 182 cm passenger ahead of the rear-facing seat and a 184 cm driver ahead of a forward-facing seat. Passenger text also says 184 cm elsewhere; retain the conservative report.

access.detail: BabyDrive found child loading from inside and outside manageable; the exact base family test reports wide-opening doors. No third row is involved.

audit.summary: Verified a mixed-facing related test, identified centre-booster exceptions and original MY21 service prices, added the selected MY23 driveshaft campaign and scoped owner sentiment. Fuel budget now uses an exact base road-test observation; uncertain annual repair and used-price assumptions remain labelled.

items.finding: A$25,888–28,990 drive-away, two distinct MY21 base cars at 54,534–123,976 km. Fresh HW3681 stock verified; cashback terms and FU34790 fresh availability need confirmation. Later-year cached listings were excluded.

Non-XT 2.5: 138 kW / 245 Nm, ADR 7.3 L/100km, minimum 91 RON. Exact base test observed 9.6 for one urban/suburban week; this now informs the editable budget, not a fleet claim. MY23 equipment changes are listed.

Related mixed-facing trial works, but restraint models are unnamed and front-passenger height is inconsistent (182/184 cm). Selected centre boosters failed ANCAP. Base-grade fit and daily booster buckles remain pending; boot is 522 L VDA.

Five years / unlimited km private-use cover transfers with the car; 12 V battery two years, ordinary wear excluded. Use the MY21-onward handbook, not the obsolete six-month-service booklet. Original VIN terms control.

12 months / 12,500 km. Original first five caps: MY21 A$2,449.88; MY25 A$2,715.67. Retain A$750/year used-car allowance. Handbook identifies coolant at 75,000 km/72 months and plugs/filter at 100,000 km/96 months; confirm due quotes.

Insurance rechecked 18 October 2026: A$1,140/year planning budget; A$750–2,500 sensitivity, not guaranteed quotes. National model mean · not a 2.5-only sample. No unsupported SUV loading. Your drivers, excess, insured value and cover still need a quote; CTP is separate.

Budget aftermarket audit, 18 October 2026. 225/60R18 104W XL replacement reference: A$756 for four fitted. Common 40,000 km life is an illustrative assumption, not model-specific wear evidence. Prices and annual savings are estimates; check the real placard and local fitted quote.

Added VIN-limited MY23 front-driveshaft recall; all four applicable campaigns have free remedies. A$1,100/year reserve retained as savings, not measured repairs. No Australian installed BT CVT/TCV quote or annual failure rate established; US extension is not local cover.

ProductReview sixth-generation 3.1/5, 25 self-selected reviews, mixes Sport/Touring/XT. Apply limited relevance to non-XT base. Add direct CarsGuide base 7.9/10 alongside existing Wheels 8.5/10; professional scores do not measure reliability.

2,000 kg braked towing / 200 kg ball limit; five seats, full-size spare. BT ANCAP five-star 2021 rating expires Dec 2027. QLD private four-cylinder renewal A$864.50–880.50 including Class 1 CTP; petrol duty differs from hybrid duty. Resale remains a scenario.
